recipes.notes: Every archive has one top-level folder (zig-<os>-<arch>-<ver>/ or zig-<arch>-<os>-<ver>/; zig-0.2.0/ for the 0.2.0 Windows zip) holding the zig binary with lib/ (and doc/, LICENSE) beside it: strip 1. No symlinks in any archive (checked all 130 listings). Tar modes must be kept (zig is 0755). NOT relocatable on its own: the binary only looks for its lib at the build machine's prefix (strace: a single access() of /root/zig-bootstrap/out/stage1/lib/zig/std/index.zig) and fails with 'Unable to find zig lib directory'. Every invocation must pass --zig-install-prefix "{runtime_dir}" (checked: build-exe of a hello world then works from a path with spaces). 0.2.0 has no global cache; the per-build cache goes to ./zig-cache unless --cache-dir is passed. No zig cc in this version. The mkdir step is only for parity with later recipes. Launch with the absolute path to the zig executable; it finds lib/ next to itself (no PATH, no registry). Clear in the app's process environment: ZIG_LIB_DIR (checked: 0.16 fails outright with ZIG_LIB_DIR=/nonexistent, so a user's global setting would hijack the private copy), ZIG_LIBC, ZIG_BUILD_RUNNER, CC, C_INCLUDE_PATH, CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH, LIBRARY_PATH and the NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE/NIX_CFLAGS_LINK/NIX_LDFLAGS trio, all of which `zig env` 0.16 lists as read (checked: C_INCLUDE_PATH is honoured by zig cc even with an explicit -target). Use `zig version` to verify, not `zig env`: env creates the global cache folder as a side effect (checked).

The global cache follows XDG_CACHE_HOME, so run zig with XDG_CACHE_HOME={runtime_dir}/cache and it lands in {runtime_dir}/cache/zig (checked on 0.6.0 and 0.7.1: nothing written to the fake HOME). Tested on amd64 0.6.0 and 0.7.1 from a path with spaces: Zig hello world, zig cc and zig c++ all built and ran. i386 0.6.0 on an amd64 kernel: Zig hello world built, but zig cc segfaulted (not investigated; may be specific to running the 32-bit binary on a 64-bit host). Other arches (arm64, armv6kz, armv7a, riscv64) are the same layout and static but were not run. {runtime_dir} is root/Administrator-owned, so {runtime_dir}/cache must be made writable by whichever account runs the app's builds (or point the cache variable at the app's own writable data folder instead; either stays inside the app). The cache is safe to share between concurrent zig processes of the same version (file locks), but should not be shared between apps if they must stay independent; deleting it is always safe. zig cc / zig c++ (0.6+) is a working C/C++ cross-compiler in this one archive (checked hello.c and hello.cpp). Caveat: with NO -target, a native Linux build detects the host glibc and puts /usr/include, /usr/include/<triple> and /usr/local/include on the include path (seen in `zig cc -v`), so native builds are not hermetic. Install size: archive ~45-55 MB xz, ~260-400 MB unpacked (0.16.0: 165 MB binary + 231 MB lib, of which lib/libc is 175 MB); the global cache then grows by roughly 25-100+ MB per target/version as libc, libc++ and compiler_rt get built on first use. Launch with the absolute path to the zig executable; it finds lib/ next to itself (no PATH, no registry). Signing: none of the macOS builds is notarized or Developer-ID signed. x86_64 binaries carry no signature at all; arm64 binaries carry only the linker's ad-hoc signature (CodeDirectory flags 0x2 adhoc, plus 0x20000 linker-signed from 0.7.0 and 0.10+, no CMS blob), which is the minimum Apple Silicon needs to execute. Gatekeeper only assesses files with the com.apple.quarantine xattr. Files the installer downloads with its own HTTP code are not quarantined unless the installer process opted in to quarantine (LSFileQuarantineEnabled) or is sandboxed; a browser download of the archive would be, and then `zig` would be refused as from an unidentified developer. The xattr step strips quarantine from the private copy only, defensively (the 2>/dev/null || true covers an absent attribute). Do not re-sign: the ad-hoc signature is valid and editing the binary would break it. zig cc is not usable before 0.6; in 0.6 it may need the Xcode command line tools for native macOS linking (not verified). Launch with the absolute path to the zig executable; it finds lib/ next to itself (no PATH, no registry). prerequisites: arm64 0.7.0 only: links the system libz.1, libxml2.2, libc++.1 and libncurses.5.4 dylibs (all shipped with macOS 11)
side_effects: run time, only if XDG_CACHE_HOME is not set for the zig process: global cache at $HOME/.cache/zig
run time: ./zig-cache in the project directory unless --cache-dir is passed
recipes.notes: Not run on macOS; the cache logic is the same resolveGlobalCacheDir (XDG_CACHE_HOME, then $HOME/.cache/zig) that was checked on Linux 0.7.1, so run zig with XDG_CACHE_HOME={runtime_dir}/cache. The arm64 build is 0.7.0 because 0.7.1 shipped none. Every archive has one top-level folder (zig-<os>-<arch>-<ver>/ or zig-<arch>-<os>-<ver>/; zig-0.2.0/ for the 0.2.0 Windows zip) holding the zig binary with lib/ (and doc/, LICENSE) beside it: strip 1. No symlinks in any archive (checked all 130 listings). Tar modes must be kept (zig is 0755). Signing: none of the macOS builds is notarized or Developer-ID signed. x86_64 binaries carry no signature at all; arm64 binaries carry only the linker's ad-hoc signature (CodeDirectory flags 0x2 adhoc, plus 0x20000 linker-signed from 0.7.0 and 0.10+, no CMS blob), which is the minimum Apple Silicon needs to execute. Gatekeeper only assesses files with the com.apple.quarantine xattr. Files the installer downloads with its own HTTP code are not quarantined unless the installer process opted in to quarantine (LSFileQuarantineEnabled) or is sandboxed; a browser download of the archive would be, and then `zig` would be refused as from an unidentified developer. The xattr step strips quarantine from the private copy only, defensively (the 2>/dev/null || true covers an absent attribute). Do not re-sign: the ad-hoc signature is valid and editing the binary would break it. Launch with the absolute path to the zig executable; it finds lib/ next to itself (no PATH, no registry). Clear in the app's process environment: ZIG_LIB_DIR (checked: 0.16 fails outright with ZIG_LIB_DIR=/nonexistent, so a user's global setting would hijack the private copy), ZIG_LIBC, ZIG_BUILD_RUNNER, CC, C_INCLUDE_PATH, CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH, LIBRARY_PATH and the NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE/NIX_CFLAGS_LINK/NIX_LDFLAGS trio, all of which `zig env` 0.16 lists as read (checked: C_INCLUDE_PATH is honoured by zig cc even with an explicit -target). Use `zig version` to verify, not `zig env`: env creates the global cache folder as a side effect (checked).
recipes.min_os: x86_64 0.7.1: macOS 10.15.7 (LC_VERSION_MIN_MACOSX; also links the system libncurses.5.4). arm64 0.7.0: macOS 11.0

launch.notes: The app is the program built by project_install and runs directly.

recipes.notes: Not run (no macOS host); from Mach-O inspection and the source. Links only libSystem. Run zig with ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR={runtime_dir}/cache. Every archive has one top-level folder (zig-<os>-<arch>-<ver>/ or zig-<arch>-<os>-<ver>/; zig-0.2.0/ for the 0.2.0 Windows zip) holding the zig binary with lib/ (and doc/, LICENSE) beside it: strip 1. No symlinks in any archive (checked all 130 listings). Tar modes must be kept (zig is 0755). Signing: none of the macOS builds is notarized or Developer-ID signed. x86_64 binaries carry no signature at all; arm64 binaries carry only the linker's ad-hoc signature (CodeDirectory flags 0x2 adhoc, plus 0x20000 linker-signed from 0.7.0 and 0.10+, no CMS blob), which is the minimum Apple Silicon needs to execute. Gatekeeper only assesses files with the com.apple.quarantine xattr. Files the installer downloads with its own HTTP code are not quarantined unless the installer process opted in to quarantine (LSFileQuarantineEnabled) or is sandboxed; a browser download of the archive would be, and then `zig` would be refused as from an unidentified developer. The xattr step strips quarantine from the private copy only, defensively (the 2>/dev/null || true covers an absent attribute). Do not re-sign: the ad-hoc signature is valid and editing the binary would break it. zig cc ships libSystem .tbd stubs and macOS libc headers from 0.9 (lib/libc/darwin; absent in 0.8.1), so plain C/C++ for macOS should build without Xcode; frameworks beyond libSystem need an SDK (not verified here). {runtime_dir} is root/Administrator-owned, so {runtime_dir}/cache must be made writable by whichever account runs the app's builds (or point the cache variable at the app's own writable data folder instead; either stays inside the app). The cache is safe to share between concurrent zig processes of the same version (file locks), but should not be shared between apps if they must stay independent; deleting it is always safe. Launch with the absolute path to the zig executable; it finds lib/ next to itself (no PATH, no registry). Clear in the app's process environment: ZIG_LIB_DIR (checked: 0.16 fails outright with ZIG_LIB_DIR=/nonexistent, so a user's global setting would hijack the private copy), ZIG_LIBC, ZIG_BUILD_RUNNER, CC, C_INCLUDE_PATH, CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH, LIBRARY_PATH and the NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE/NIX_CFLAGS_LINK/NIX_LDFLAGS trio, all of which `zig env` 0.16 lists as read (checked: C_INCLUDE_PATH is honoured by zig cc even with an explicit -target). Use `zig version` to verify, not `zig env`: env creates the global cache folder as a side effect (checked).
